'''Adatara Shrine''' (あだたらじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} located in {{ill|Motomiya, Fukushima|Q867106|qid=Q867106}}, {{ill|Fukushima Prefecture|Q71707|qid=Q71707}}. It is a candidate shrine of Iitoyowa-ke Shrine, a {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=listed minor shrine}}. Under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|lt=former shrine ranking}}, it was classified as a Prefectural Shrine.

=== Overview ===
The shrine is said to have been founded in {{ill|1146|Q19627|qid=Q19627}} (Kyūan 2) during the {{ill|Heian period|Q193292|qid=Q193292}}. It is believed to have begun when the deities of {{ill|Mount Adatara|Q352675|qid=Q352675}} and Mount Ōnagura were enshrined and established as a satomiya (village shrine). Locals affectionately call it “Myōjin-sama.” As it is regarded as the head shrine of the Adatara Shrines scattered throughout the surrounding area, it is said that the name of the place of enshrinement changed from “Motome Village” to Motomiya Village, becoming the origin of the place name “Motomiya.” It was also once the chief guardian shrine of the former Adachi District; however, in {{ill|1683|Q7651|qid=Q7651|lt=Tenna 3}}, Suzuki Aki-no-Kami, a priest of {{ill|Nihonmatsu Shrine|Q22119901|qid=Q22119901|lt=formerly Nihonmatsu Kumano Shrine}} (the present Nihonmatsu Shrine), argued that “the enshrined deity of Adatara Shrine is the spirit of a person named Adachi Tarō, not the deities of Mount Adatara, and therefore it is not suitable to be the district’s chief guardian shrine.” As a result, the then chief priest, Takahashi Jibu Shōsuke, was dismissed from his position as “Shimenegashira,” the coordinating head of the district’s priests, and Adatara Shrine was stripped of its title as the chief guardian shrine of Adachi District. <ref>“Illustrated History of Motomiya,” Chapter 3, Section 17</ref>

=== Festival Dates ===
* May 1
* Three days from the fourth Friday of October

At the Spring Festival on May 1, parishioners of Ukishima Shrine in the Shirazawa area of Motomiya City dedicate “Daidai Kagura.”

During the Autumn Festival in October, three {{ill|Taikodai|Q11444734|qid=Q11444734}} floats traditionally handed down in areas of the former {{ill|Nihonmatsu Domain|Q909007|qid=Q909007|lt=Nihonmatsu Domain territory}} appear and parade through the town ahead of the mikoshi procession.

=== Access ===
* Nearest station: {{ill|East Japan Railway Company|Q499071|qid=Q499071|lt=JR East}} {{ill|Tōhoku Main Line|Q681190|qid=Q681190}} {{ill|Motomiya Station|Q873962|qid=Q873962|lt=Motomiya Station}} (15 minutes on foot)
